name: V3205SD
full_name: 4096-Stage Low-Voltage Low-Noise BBD Analog Delay Line
description: 4096-stage bucket-brigade delay line running on a single low positive supply (5V typical), giving 20.48ms to 204.8ms of analog delay. A charge packet is passed capacitor to capacitor by a two-phase clock, so the signal stays analog end to end: sampled in time, never quantized. Coolaudio's in-production replacement for the Panasonic MN3205.

extra.clock_range: 10 to 100kHz (delay = stages / (2 x clock); 204.8ms at a 10kHz clock)
extra.supply: VDD = +5V typ (4 to 8V); VGG = 14/15 x VDD
extra.abs_max: -0.3 to +11V on VDD, VGG, CP and input

typical_application: Analog delay, echo, chorus, flanger and reverb. Delay = stages / (2 x clock), so 4096 stages at a 10kHz clock gives 204.8ms. The full recipe is V3205 + a V3102 clock driver + a V571 compander, which is the classic analog-delay pedal signal chain.
gotchas: it does nothing on its own: it needs a two-phase non-overlapping clock. Pair it with a V3102/MN3102 clock driver, which also generates the VGG bias
NOT a drop-in for the MN3005. The MN3005 runs a negative supply (VDD = -15V); the V3205 is a positive low-voltage part (4 to 8V). It replaces the MN3205
companding is effectively mandatory: compress in and expand out with a V571/NE571, or the noise floor of 4096 charge transfers dominates
the clock sets delay AND bandwidth at once (Nyquist = clock/2), so longer delays lose high end; anti-alias filter going in and reconstruction filter coming out
OUT1 and OUT2 are one stage apart; designs typically sum them to help cancel clock feedthrough
VGG is a bias input, not a second rail: it sits at 14/15 of VDD
notes: Pins and specs checked against Coolaudio's own V3205SD datasheet (V1.0), supplied by the user. Note reseller listings for this part are unreliable: several claim DIP-14 and S/N 67dB, while the manufacturer's sheet says an 8-lead DIP, 4-8V, and S/N 60dB.
